methods.label: Use the hypotenuse midpoint
methods.explanation:
The altitude creates a right triangle whose hypotenuse has midpoint \(M\), so the hypotenuse-midpoint property can give us equal sides.

Since \(AH\) is an altitude, \(AH\perp BC\). The angles at \(B\) and \(C\) are both acute, so \(H\) lies between \(B\) and \(C\). Since \(BM\) is a median, \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AC\).

Thus \(AC\) is the hypotenuse of right triangle \(AHC\). The segment from a right-angle vertex to the midpoint of the hypotenuse equals half the hypotenuse, so
\[
HM=\frac{AC}{2}=CM.
\]
Triangle \(HMC\) is therefore isosceles, with equal angles opposite \(HM\) and \(CM\). Because the rays \(CM\) and \(CA\) coincide, and the rays \(CH\) and \(CB\) coincide,
\[
\angle MHC=\angle MCH=\angle ACB=30^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{30^\circ}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
